summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and recent coronary artery bypass graft complicated by saphenous vein graft infection was readmitted for evaluation of atypical chest pain. The pain was burning in nature, occurred when lying down, and resolved upon sitting, raising concern for both cardiac ischemia and GERD. Workup showed no EKG changes, stable troponins, and no arrhythmias on telemetry, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. A chest X-ray revealed stable pleural effusions and atelectasis. The pain was attributed to GERD, possibly exacerbated by recent dietary intake. He remained on IV antibiotics for the ongoing graft infection per protocol and received scheduled hemodialysis. His condition improved, and he was discharged home on stable medications, including the addition of carvedilol, with instructions to monitor symptoms and follow up with his care team.
